title: The Setup Checklist: From 0 Calls on Monday to a Steady Calendar in 6 Weeks
description: A week-by-week checklist to go from zero booked calls to a steady calendar with cold email: the list, the inbox setup, and daily volume.
lead: This is the full setup checklist from the reel. You get the 3 steps (a list of people who fit, a setup that lands in the inbox, volume every day) as a week-by-week checklist from week 0 to week 6, a worked example, a 20-minute Monday routine, a problem finder and a prompt that plans your weeks for you.
insider: This checklist is how we run steady campaigns for clients. In our full-quarter case study, sending the same way every week from January to March brought in **1,061 interested leads from 236,545 emails**, with no big pushes and no empty weeks. The tactic is the easy part; the full system (list, inboxes, follow-ups) is what we do for clients.

blocks.text: The short answer

Your Monday has 0 calls. The company in the reel, a home services business that used to rely on Facebook ads, booked **about 29 calls a month** with cold email. That's about 7 a week. The gap isn't luck. It's three things done in order:

items: **A list of people who fit.** The right companies and the right person at each one.
**A setup that lands in the inbox.** Separate domains, authenticated, warmed up.
**Volume, every day.** The same amount of new people reached every working day, with follow-ups.

blocks.text: Done in order, this takes **about 6 weeks** from zero to full volume: 2 weeks of building and warm-up, a 3-week ramp, then steady sending. The checklist below covers each week.
Where are you now?
Answer these 6 questions. Every "no" is where you start.

head: Question
If no, start at
rows: Can you describe your best buyer in one sentence (industry, size, title, place)?
Do you have at least 2,000 verified people who match it?
Do you send from separate domains, not your main one?
Do those domains have SPF, DKIM and DMARC?
Have the inboxes been warming up for 2+ weeks?
Do you reach new people every working day, with 2 follow-ups?

blocks.text: Step 1: A list of people who fit

**Why it matters:** nobody outside your list can ever book a call. And a list of people who don't fit gets replies like "not interested" or no replies at all, which also hurts your sending reputation. Fit beats size.

**Exactly how:** write the one-sentence buyer description, pull companies that match, find 1 or 2 decision makers per company, verify every email, and note 2 real details about each company. Details matter: in [Hunter's State of Email Outreach 2026](https://hunter.io/the-state-of-cold-email), emails with two custom details got **5.6% replies vs 3.6%** without.
Step 2: A setup that lands in the inbox

**Why it matters:** an email in spam is an email nobody reads. The big providers now check every sender. [Google](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126) requires SPF or DKIM from everyone, all three (SPF, DKIM and DMARC) from bulk senders, and a spam rate below **0.3%** (it recommends under 0.1%). [Microsoft](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoftthreatprotectionblog/strengthening-email-ecosystem-outlook%E2%80%99s-new-requirements-for-high%E2%80%90volume-senders/4399730) requires SPF, DKIM and DMARC for domains sending over 5,000 emails a day to Outlook.com.

**Exactly how:** separate sending domains, up to 3 inboxes per domain, the three DNS records on each, and warm-up turned on before any cold email goes out. [Instantly's 2026 benchmark report](https://instantly.ai/cold-email-benchmark-report-2026) says to start at 5 to 10 emails a day and build up over **4 to 6 weeks**.
Step 3: Volume, every day

**Why it matters:** one big send fills one week. Steady sending fills every week. Instantly found that teams who send consistently get **15 to 20% more replies**, and that bursty sending (500 one day, nothing for three days, then 1,000) looks suspicious to providers. Follow-ups matter too: **42% of replies** in Instantly's data came after the first email.
**Exactly how:** the same daily limit on every inbox, Monday to Friday. New people added every day. Every person gets 3 emails, 3 to 4 days apart.

blocks.text: Week 0: The list

items: Write your buyer sentence: "[Job title] at [type of company] with [size] in [place]."
List 3 problems this buyer has that you solve. Pick the biggest one for email 1.
Pull matching companies from a lead database, Google Maps or industry directories.
Find 1 or 2 decision makers per company with work emails.
Verify every email. Remove anything that's invalid or risky.
Add 2 real details per company in your sheet (what they do, a recent change, where they work).
Check the count against your goal (see the worked example below).

blocks.text: Week 1: The setup

items: Buy separate sending domains that look like your brand. Never use your main domain.
Buy 1 or 2 spare domains as backups.
Create up to 3 inboxes per domain, each with a real name and photo.
Add SPF, DKIM and DMARC to every domain. Our [DNS guide](/blog/dns-records-for-cold-email.html) has the records.
Point each sending domain to your real website.
Connect every inbox to your sending tool and turn warm-up on.
Add each domain to [Google Postmaster Tools](https://postmaster.google.com) so you can see spam rates later.

blocks.text: Week 2: Warm-up and the emails

items: Leave warm-up running. Send zero cold emails this week.
Write the 3-email sequence (use the prompt below). Email 1 under 80 words.
Add a plain way to say no to each email, like "Not for you? Reply no and I won't email again."
Remove links and images from email 1.
Send the sequence to yourself on Gmail and Outlook. Read it on your phone.
Set the schedule: Monday to Friday, during your buyers' work hours, 3 to 4 days between emails.

blocks.text: Week 3 and 4: The ramp

items: Week 3: 10 cold emails per inbox per day. Week 4: 20 per inbox per day.
Launch new people on Monday. Instantly's data shows Monday is a good day to start sequences and Wednesday gets the most replies.
Check bounces every day. Over 2%? Stop that list and verify it again.
Answer every interested reply within a few hours. Offer one specific time.
Log every reply: interested, not now, wrong person, no.

blocks.text: Week 5 and after: Full volume

items: 30 cold emails per inbox per day, every weekday. Keep warm-up on.
Add new people every day so first emails never stop.
Order the next list when the current one is 75% used.
Run the Monday routine below, every week.

blocks.text: Worked example: from 0 to 5 calls a week

Say your goal is **5 booked calls a week** (about 22 a month: 5 × 4.33 = 21.7). Use a starting guess of **2 calls per 1,000 people**. Here's where it comes from: Hunter's average is 45 replies per 1,000 people (4.5%). In our [full-quarter case study](/results.html#case-04) about 1 in 4 replies was interested, so about 11. In our [5-day blitz](/results.html#case-03) about 1 in 5 interested people booked (25 of 115), so about 2.

items: New people needed each week: 5 calls ÷ 2 per 1,000 = **2,500 people a week**.
Each gets 3 emails: 2,500 × 3 = **7,500 emails a week** once you're at full volume.
Per working day: 7,500 ÷ 5 = **1,500 emails a day**.
Inboxes at 30 a day each: 1,500 ÷ 30 = **50 inboxes**.
Domains at 3 inboxes each: 50 ÷ 3 = 16.7, so **17 domains**, plus 2 spares = 19.
List for the first month: 2,500 × 4 weeks = **10,000 verified people**, so build at least 2,000 to 3,000 in week 0 and keep adding.

blocks.label: Replace the guess with your numbers
blocks.text: After your first 1,000 people, divide calls booked by people reached. That's your real number. Rerun the math with it.
The 20-minute Monday routine
Do this every Monday, before you launch the week's new people. It keeps the calendar full and catches problems before they cost you a domain.

blocks.text: Common mistakes

items: **Skipping week 0.** Buying inboxes before you know who you're emailing.
**Sending in week 1.** New domains need warm-up first. Rushing burns them.
**Stopping after email 1.** You lose the 42% of replies that come from follow-ups.
**Sending only when you have time.** Steady beats bursts, in replies and in deliverability.
**Judging it in week 3.** The ramp is not full volume. Judge results from week 6 on.

blocks.text: Let Claude plan your 6 weeks

blocks.label: 6-week plan prompt (copy it)
blocks.text:
Help me plan a cold email setup from zero to a steady calendar.

My buyer: [job title] at [type of company] with [size] in [place]
What I sell: [one sentence]
Calls I want per week: [number]
Start date (a Monday): [date]
My starting guess: [2] calls per 1,000 people reached (change it if you have real numbers)

Rules: every person gets 3 emails, 3-4 days apart. Max 30 cold emails per inbox per day, max 3 inboxes per domain, plus 2 spare domains. Weeks 1-2 warm-up only (no cold emails), then 10 / 20 / 30 emails per inbox per day in weeks 3, 4 and 5. Send Monday to Friday only.

Give me:
1) people needed per week, emails per day, inboxes and domains (round up, show the math),
2) a week-by-week checklist with dates for weeks 0 to 6,
3) how many verified people I need before week 3,
4) a Monday checklist with these limits: bounce rate under 2%, spam rate under 0.1%.

faq.q: Can I skip the warm-up if I'm in a hurry?
faq.a: Don't. New domains that send lots of cold email right away look like spammers. Instantly says to build up over 4 to 6 weeks. Skipping it can cost you the domains and the weeks anyway.

faq.q: How many people do I need on my list to start?
faq.a: Enough for the ramp plus a buffer. In the worked example, that's 2,500 new people a week at full volume. Start with at least 2,000 to 3,000 verified people and keep adding every week.
It's a natural start for the week. Instantly's data shows Monday is a good day to launch new sequences and Wednesday gets the most replies. Use Monday for your routine and new batches.

faq.q: What if I only want 1 or 2 calls a week?
faq.a: Use the same steps with smaller numbers. At 2 calls per 1,000 people, 2 calls a week is about 1,000 new people a week, 3,000 emails a week, 600 a day and 20 inboxes.
